_meta.what_this_is: A small, transparent, hand-authored set of famous ads encoded as Yeo-7 network-activation descriptors, paired with publicly-reported outcome magnitudes. It is fed through the REAL local neurosignal construct engine (neurosignal.detect.detect_from_networks) to produce buy/sell + approach scores.
_meta.what_this_is_NOT: This is NOT measured brain data and NOT the Mary/TRIBE encoder. The network activations are structured expert descriptors of each ad's dominant neural drivers, on a common 0-1 axis, scored with normalize=False so ads are comparable to each other. Treat every number as an ILLUSTRATIVE, predicted-construct estimate on n=8. It demonstrates the scoring machinery and the investor-facing story shape; it is not validation of the predicted-brain -> behavior link (see neurosignal/CHAIN_AUDIT_2026-07-16.md, 'Link 4').
_meta.descriptor_axis: Each network value in 0..1 estimates that Yeo-7 network's relative engagement by the ad, from its documented creative structure (fear appeal, reward imagery, motion/attention, narrative memory). Rationale is stored per-ad so the mapping is auditable and editable.
_meta.outcome_axis: outcome_magnitude is a coarse, publicly-reported effect size (vote swing, brand-lift, or documented sales/recall lift), normalized to 0..1 for plotting. Sources are cited. These are approximate and heterogeneous across campaigns; the cross-ad correlation is illustrative only.

ads.name: Daisy (LBJ, 1964)
ads.rationale: Nuclear fear appeal: peak amygdala/limbic threat + salience/interrupt (VentralAttention), countdown drives dorsal attention; low deliberation.
ads.outcome_source: Widely credited with a large persuasion effect; magnitude is a historical estimate (aired once, dominated coverage). Approximate.

ads.name: 1984 (Apple, Super Bowl)
ads.rationale: High cinematic visual salience + attention capture (the runner/hammer), moderate emotional arousal, strong narrative-memory imprint.
ads.outcome_source: Frequently cited as a landmark brand-lift ad (Macintosh launch). Magnitude approximate/qualitative.

ads.name: Think Small (VW, 1959)
ads.rationale: Cognitive/witty print appeal: deliberation-forward (Frontoparietal), memorable framing (Default), low arousal/salience.
ads.outcome_source: Canonically effective long-run brand campaign; magnitude qualitative/approximate.

ads.name: Morning in America (Reagan, 1984)
ads.rationale: Warm-emotion + autobiographical/narrative (Default) reassurance imagery; moderate salience, low conflict.
ads.outcome_source: Associated with a strong incumbent cycle; ad-specific effect is an approximate historical estimate.

ads.name: Whopper Freakout (BK, 2007)
ads.rationale: Surprise/violation salience (VentralAttention) with social-proof emotion; documented sales response.
ads.outcome_source: Reported double-digit sales lift in case writeups; normalized approximate.

ads.name: Generic product spot (low-arousal control)
ads.rationale: Flat informational spot: low arousal, low salience, low memory imprint. Included as a low-outcome anchor.
ads.outcome_source: Synthetic low-anchor control, not a real campaign. Labeled as control.

ads.name: Fear-appeal PSA (anti-smoking, graphic)
ads.rationale: Strong threat/disgust limbic drive + salience; graphic anti-smoking PSAs show measurable recall/quit-intent.
ads.outcome_source: Graphic-warning PSA literature reports meaningful recall/quit-intent lifts; normalized approximate.

ads.name: Dumb Ways to Die (Metro, 2012)
ads.rationale: Catchy narrative-memory (Default) + charming visual encoding; documented awareness/behavioral pledge lift.
ads.outcome_source: Case reports cite large awareness and pledge-to-be-safe lifts; normalized approximate.
